reviews.text: Interesting lane-ways of stores, dining establishments and street food type stalls. Lots of the outlets are almost duplicates of others, lots of tea, trinkets, white rabbit candy outlets, smaller food retailers. Interesting for a walk, one visit is fine.

Small lanes with retail and cafes lining the area. We went in the afternoon and it was cool as it was cloudy today. There is a large mall with plenty of restaurants to pick from also. There are public toilets in the area and if you cant find it, ask the vendors for directions or spot the lime green signage

Tianzifang feels more like a checklist stop than a genuine highlight. While it’s often described as a charming arts-and-crafts quarter, the reality is fairly average: narrow, enclosed lanes that limit views, creating a sense of congestion rather than discovery. The layout makes it hard to linger comfortably, and the overall experience feels more compressed than atmospheric. The food and shops are similarly so-so, with limited variety and a strong sense of repetition from stall to stall. Nothing is particularly bad, but very little stands out either, especially when compared to other parts of Shanghai that offer better design, stronger curation, or more breathing space. If time is tight, Tianzifang is an easy place to skip without much regret.
Too many people (China Public holiday cum Weekends). There souvenirs, pubs and food here. Prices is rasonable too except clothing :) Its gonna be hot, so wear appropriately
A charming maze of narrow lanes filled with art studios, cafés, boutiques, and street vibes. Very atmospheric and fun to walk around. Great for photos and discovering local creativity.
This is one of the most vibrating part of ShangHai. It is a Maze of small streets full of design clothing or fancy souvenirs plus some bohemian pubs. Nice place to chill for a while
Nice place for leisure walk. The alleys are narrow but full of character. Souvenir shops and restaurants can be found here.

Came here in Nove 2024 and the weather was good... despite quite a lot of people, this place was several entrance and exit points. Whichever you enter or exit, it is a cool place to visit, buy some souvenir which I did and if you have difficulties paying using your e-wallet, don't get panic, they offer you WiFi for better connectivity especially when you're using roaming. The sellers are really nice and they comprised of small stores of all variety of items you could and couldn't think of. If you have chance, dropby any tea house and they will offer you a cup of tea. After that, you will be captivated with their tea and you will buy.. 😆 frankly the items are really affordable and not overly priced.

This tourist hotspot lives up to its reputation. Yes, it's crowded and commercial, but the experience justifies the visit. You'll find plenty of souvenir shops and quick dining options scattered throughout. Timing matters—visit early or late to avoid the heaviest crowds. Don't skip the historical information available on-site. Learning the backstory makes the visit much more meaningful. Worth the trip despite the touristic feel.

This old are used to have lots of family businesses. Today it’s full of small shops and restaurants. And here is also some galleries and artists. Weekends it can be crowded so if you can go here during the week. Great for buying souvenirs, cards and eat something. It’s a very charming area, even if it’s nowadays very touristy. It’s famous as an art area, and I think it’s worth a visit.

This is considered the super artsy street but it's very touristy (and not artsy in my opinion). I was imagining more local artists and murals and such. Lots of branded stuff but definitely more local than a mall. I saw maybe 3 tour groups when here by myself. Overpriced area but nice to walk. Can't say that I'd come again. People do live in the neighborhood so please be respectful of noise and such!

blew me away. It is full of alleys, a veritable little labyrinth in which it is easy to get lost, but everything is so beautiful, colorful and charming that you don't mind wandering around. It is full of shops, studios, where they make you pearl bracelets on the spot, they mix a mixture of herbs for tea, there are galleries, souvenirs, cafes, street food. A nice surprise awaits you around every corner. I enjoyed it.

Things are very much for the tourists and many duplicates. Example, few shops selling the same rabbit candies. Mouldy smell in small alley. Overall, for experience or photo takings. The place is not that big but walking along the road you may reach more heritage places. So it might just be a part of the itinerary but not the main highlight. If this is the first stop. Then take line 9. Besides there is a huge shopping mall.

It's a totally different world when you hit the ally. I was amazed by how narrow the Lane is but yet you will find it can be so crowded with people. Visit weekdays for less crowds. PH and the weekend is crowded. The scene along the way there, trees along both sides of the roads makes walking there enjoyable. A MUST VISIT.

Tianzifang, tucked away in Shanghai’s former French Concession, is a maze of narrow alleys lined with old Shikumen houses that have been transformed into boutiques, galleries, and cafés. Unlike the polished redevelopment of Xintiandi, Tianzifang has a more authentic, lived-in charm—laundry still hangs above the lanes, and the atmosphere mixes local life with a creative, artsy vibe. The market is best known for its quirky shops and art studios, selling everything from handmade crafts and paintings to unusual souvenirs you won’t find in big malls. Alongside the shopping, there’s a huge variety of food options: cozy coffee shops, teahouses, bars, and international restaurants tucked into the alleyways. It’s a great place for wandering, people-watching, and café-hopping while soaking up the retro-chic setting. That said, Tianzifang can get very crowded, especially on weekends or evenings, and prices are higher than in less touristy parts of the city. Still, it’s one of the most atmospheric spots in Shanghai to explore—perfect if you want to experience old-Shanghai architecture blended with modern creativity and a lively street culture.
Old Shanghai with many interesting alleys and shops The place to buy Chinese traditional dresses and shirts

This is an easy place to get to via the Metro. Spent a few hours exploring this tourist destination. There are some interesting shops and sights but there are certainly some repeat shops and themes. It is worth visiting if you are in the area and have not been before, but you will not have missed anything if you never visit. Quite a few food stalls selling standard street food. All look good and the few stalls I tried tasted ok too. Had the tofu, fried squid, and a coffee. Went to the shopping center above the metro for dinner.
Very beautiful... it was like to walk in a dream... street are very small with a lot of shops. We went there in afternoon, but at night would be more beatiful I think

First time in sh. I enjoyed walking around and looking at the cute shops. Also bought very fragrant teas, ate very delicious xiao long bao at a small corner shop. Definitely recommend this dumpling shop by the way. Even my sh friend commented on how good it was.
Came here but it was pourrrriiiing. Was impossible to walk around. But managed to browse cute tea store and have some desserts around!
A cute shopping area with small alleyway shops selling food, clothes, tea, and other random stuff 😁

Tianzifang is a must-visit spot in Shanghai for anyone who loves artsy vibes and local culture. Tucked into old alleyways, it’s full of unique boutiques, craft shops, cozy cafes, and galleries. What makes it special is how it blends the traditional Shikumen architecture with a creative, modern twist. It’s not just a shopping spot—it’s a glimpse into Shanghai’s artistic soul and a great place to wander, explore, and soak in the city’s charm.

Very pretty streets full of interesting shops selling souvenirs, clothing and other arts knic knacs. Buildings architecture is beautiful 😍 and has a great laid back vibe. Walk in between the narrow streets to see a surprise round each corner. Some great cafe options and near a metro stop, so it is easy to get to. Recommend a short 2hr visit and go early to avoid crowds.

it's a old, dark and narrow lane (backstreet?!) with some small shops there selling souvenirs and accessories. but the shops are quite repeating - rabbit milk candies, soaps, some ceramic cup and fake jades. they may look interesting to tourist that first visit but soon losing interests when walking along. one thing good in here is the shops don't need to bargain, they're with marked price. overall the place is very cheap and commercial. not recommended.

Small little district that gives different vibes in the day and night. Narrow alleys and shops peddling similar souvenirs, cheongsams, handicraft, some food stalls and a few bars littled around. I like that it's not too big and you can cover most of it in an hour or two.

Tianzifang is a lively and fascinating area in Shanghai, known for its narrow alleyways filled with unique shops, art studios, and cafes. The atmosphere is vibrant and full of energy, making it a great place to explore. One of the main attractions of Tianzifang is the variety of small boutiques offering handmade crafts, jewelry, and other interesting items. It’s a perfect spot for finding unique gifts and souvenirs. The area also has a strong artistic vibe, with many galleries and studios showcasing local art. It’s a great place to experience the creative side of Shanghai. Overall, Tianzifang is a must-visit for anyone in Shanghai looking to experience a different side of the city. It’s full of charm and always has something new to discover.

Had a great time visiting this quaint shopping and cultural part of Shanghai. Lot's of small shops with plenty to offer, although some shops offer very similar items. Food is also offered here, and there's plenty of options around each corner. Nice place for some photos, and also just to stop for a drink as well. Not necessarily a tourist spot, but recommended coming during lunch or late afternoon for a nice experience and wasn't too crowded either. Save about 1-2h to browse through everything, should be more than enough.

"Shaghai's well kept art and craft enclave" Most of the area around Shanghai was renovated as a plan of city development however Tianzifang is the only place which keeps its old heritage till now. Walking along the way I could see lot of art stores, bars, design stores, restaurants on either sides of the road. The historic buildings are still maintained and most of the place is filled with art galleries promoting their sales. Even though this is one of the main tourist spots in Shanghai and has lot of crowd all through out the day but its still kept well clean and maintained, even the smaller streets around this area. I was walking along the street going through every snack stores and trying out their free samples. I really enjoy spending time in places like these. This is a small place and the amount of time can be spent can not be estimated. By looking at the restaurants &a bars it was safe to say that this is a place of interest for foreigners than the locals. Most of them either enjoying the food & beverages while reading books and somewhere enjoying the art and interacting with the artists.

It’s sort of like maze of little cafe, small boutique shops, restaurants, and bars. Each of the different streets have very nice designs and a nice place to hang out and look for souvenirs to take home.
There's nothing interesting there. The location is far from pubic transportation.

It's actually not very big an area and easily covered on foot. Nearest metro is Dapuqiao on line 9. A few small places with western food other than the local ones. We ate the grilled meat skewers and naan bread which was halal, at the end of lane with exit no. 3. Many boutiques selling Chinese ladies' clothes and stuff. Beware the shops offering "free" samples of tea infusions, unless you really like the tea and don't mind buying. They are not cheap and can cost CNY300 for a packet weighing 300g.
Most shops sell similar items. Can visit if you're around the area. Something like a street market area.

Tianzifang is one of the popular tourist destinations in Shanghai for shopping and experiencing local culture and lifestyle. It is located in the old French concession area. The area has mainly retained the "authentic and original" feeling because it has not been reconstructed or rebuilt. Instead visitors will get to see buildings, shophouses, alleys and streets of the old French concession area with Chinese "culture". It has now become famous as a "rabbit warren" of arts and crafts shops, with restaurants, bars, cafes, souvenir and boutique shops etc. It has become touristy but still a good place to have a feel of the local touch. I enjoy walking around in the small lanes around the old ancient buildings with beautiful decorations as it is quite difficult to find them these days due to the city redevelopment!
The place itself is nice, but it’s clearly tourist-oriented. Basically no one was there.
Not sure what culture or remnants of french concession you can find here, I just see refurbished old buildings with tourist focused shops. Definitely a tourist trap.

used to be super crowded with tourists just few years ago before covid, now the whole street is empty with many shops closed :( still have some souvenir shops, leather shops, tea shops and some food stalls. worth a visit if youre in town

Very nice market in the old Shanghai Street maze. It might feel a bit as a tourist trap but it’s worth going just to get the idea of the old times. Moreover, some shops are really nice and you can find typical souvenirs with a bit more local flair. Here no bargaining and you can pay with card in most shops. Many restaurants or food stands as well. Close to the metro stop.
A small tourist area with many souvenir shops and eateries selling traditional food. There are some pubs too. Not very crowded

A great multicultural streets where the French Concession used to be in 1850 - 1940s. The area have been transformed by younger generations local businesses into an artsy area comprising a multitude of craft stores, bars, cafes, studios, and boutiques. I highly recommend visiting this area for tourists who wants to enjoy a modern take of Chinese fusion culture as well as doing some gifts shopping. Though the prices are a bit more premium compared to other traditional market, it has that unique vibrant feeling that invites you to shop.
Touristy but worth a visit to grab some souvenirs . Some quaint bars and tea shops to chill .
One of my favorite places to visit in Shanghai, it is just so picturesque! Nice little shops, well decorated alleys, great snacks around and so perfect for taking pictures!

Shanghai is a great city of contrasts. Go to the bund for hyper modern skyscrapers, and later on talk a quiet stroll through the historic Tian Zi Fang district with its old townhouses and cute cafes. Highly recommended for a relaxing afternoon.

This is a nice market and a maze of narrow streets and alley ways in a relatively small area. Many of the shops carry the same items so it is worth browsing through if you have the time. Some of the shops welcome bargaining, some do not and will politely inform you via sign or words. It doesn't hurt to ask. There are a lot of restaurants, food stands, and beverage spots, too, so no need to leave the area if you're hungry. There are some one of a kind shops, too, with no other locations in Shanghai, and it is a fun challenge to remember their locations.

10 years ago it was a nice place, but in the meantime it became a very touristic place where you pay 4 times more for food and drinks than comparable restaurants. The location itself is very nice and still worth to go around and have a look.
Quaint shops that are so cute and very pretty. Some stores take VISA so that's really nice. Good unique food and the store owners are very nice and speak basic English.

If you're visiting Shanghai for the first time, don't miss the opportunity to come here and walk around these narrow alleys, you'll find tons of souvenirs, coffee shops, artworks, street food, clothes, private cinema, restaurant, even a Cat Cafe. I'm a resident here and I never get tired of coming back, there's always something new going on. Weekends are particularly harsh to walk through the crowd, try to come during week days, if possible.

Really cool place. lots of boutique shops and restaurants/ cafes. Also has some bars and dessert stalls. Has a really old time Shanghai feel. It has been revamped, but not too much as to preserve the historic feel.

A really pretty place, with all kinds of stores from cloths, food to even cat cafe. A good place for tourist to buy some souvenirs. The other problem is there’s too many people, can’t focus on taking pictures without blocking others’ way

This little part of shanghai is a throwback in time, no streets just walkways that crisscross through hundreds of little shops/ restaurants. I love it, I always bring newcomers to this exciting and bustling little part of town.

A very touristy place with plenty of snacks and street food available at a higher price. However the food are surprisingly good. Would recommend to visit if you’ve not been here before. I’ve personally been here a few times and the only reason I’ve returned is because of a tea shop named 延乐茶集 they sell all types of tea leaves, from cheap to exp. tea are mostly planted locally by the owner’s father, and you can taste any types of tea before buying.

Cute but Optional Tianzifang is a maze of narrow alleys filled with small shops selling souvenirs, handmade crafts, and cute trinkets. It’s a nice place to wander around, snap some photos, and browse if you enjoy quirky boutiques and artsy vibes. However, since its a tourist spot, items sold are often overpriced. Do come on a weekday to avoid crowds. Worth a quick stop if you’re nearby or have extra time, but not a must-see if you’re on a tight schedule.
Such a neat little district. All cobblestone, no cars. Tons of little shops and restaurants. Definitely worth a visit! Check out the I Love Shanghai Lounge, best dive in Shanghai.
Very nice old neighbourhood stores. Good for shopping. Visited heavily by the local folks, rates seemed good. Very interesting set of items and foods.
be careful everything sold here is overpriced! Look at the pictures. See how I got scammed

Little, cute streets with lots of little things, drinks, and food to try! It's a very clean, busy street, and this is as most authentic of a vibe you can get in Shanghai. Anything that are sold here are a bit more expensive than other places, but still a good place to walk around both during the day and night.
It's one of the charm of Shanghai. Small alleys filled up with cool and chic shops, colorful stuffs and variety of mouth-watering street food and snacks. Always crowded but worth visiting.

Went on a Sunday. Small alleys packed with people. Many small shops, some very interesting. There are also many eateries around. Not an easy place to navigate as some alleys leads to a dead end. Can spend hours walking here and feel lost.

Although it's become very turist-y, Tianzifang still carries the artisty, crafty feeling that made it first famous 10 or so years ago. It's full of shops of any type now, from kitch souvenirs to high quality ceramics and silks, and I think it's worth a visit if you want to see a typical old Shanghai area (people still live here, by the way, so keep that in mind when visiting very early or very late). I especially like to wander around the small alleys after 8PM, when the crowds leave😃
If you are into small boutique (though many of them sell similar stuff) in an old town ambience, then this might be for you. Gets quite crowded as it is a tourist's favorite!

Pretty from the outside but not much to see inside. It's mostly shops with repeating themes like the rabbit milk candy. Found a cool shop with really cute pins though. You can just take a few pictures and leave, and definitely skippable.

Great spot to visit! You can easily get lost wandering around the little allies. The prices are slightly high, as it's a touristy spot, but some places you can haggle to get a better price. There is a public bathroom at the entrance.

Many shops!! Bargaining place..alot traditional Chinese things shops available.. Miniso store is there!! Indian Restaurant present in the street. Old Chinese look of street. Good people. Problem for any foreigners are Chinese as very less people know English.

Tainzifang (Chinese: 田子坊) is an art resort developed from old residential area. Lots of food and souvenir shops in this area for visitors window-shopping while enjoying the ancient building. This area contains many style of building, including Eclectic, new Renaissance, modernism, Chinese traditional brick and wood structure, Spanish style, British castle style, baroque various styles. Enjoy it!!!
This is a dope little area to explore. Tons of awesome shops and places to get a drink or some food. A must.
Very different with Instagram. But it's oke to spent time in here. So many shops and cafe.

Look up... dont just focus on the shops around you.. the ambiance is better as you look up. Each will see something different based on one's background. A place in Shanghai that is deserving of 3 hours of your time. Easily accessible from Dapuqiao Subway Station - Line 9 to stop "Dapuqiao 打浦桥” - Take Exit 1
I loved this place , Its authentic Chinese place with lots of food and shopping options in cheaper price. It's very old place from Shanghai. It's near to metro station.

Small alley in the heart of Shanghai. The old buildings are renovated to small shophouses selling street food, handmade handicrafts, restaurants, souvenir shops, etc. Interesting and not-to-miss attraction. Good place for photography.
super busy, very touristy... the shops dont sell anything super unique or fancy.. consider skipping, unless you really want that one photo

Amazing place where you can appreciate the real culture of China, you can enjoy delicious food, buy presents, I did the Pearl tea tour what I highly recommend if you go to Shanghai. It is a very memorable experience for me. 👌🎊
Great area with small shops and snack/drink places. Lovely designed with lantern and corful paintings.
Loved this place. Probably lesser crowd as we went on Monday afternoon. Simply roam around and check out the souvenirs, arts and nice old style decoration. Some cafes and bars within the compound.
Very interesting place to visit in shanghai. Small ally ways lead to unexpected stores and restaurants. Lots of small stores. Kinda touristy but you can find plenty locals here too.
Traditional open air market with nice stores for handcrafts, bars and food!!! Pretty beautiful.💯

Touristy and over-commercialized Tianzifang is only good for getting a few nice photos, or for buying some cheap trinkets. The restaurants are horrible, in service, quality and price, and it's the only place in Shanghai where there have actually been restaurant staff actively trying to get you into the restaurants.
An interesting shopping maze area. Shops are selling many interesting stuff, drinks and snacks. The only down side is the crowd. It's way too crowded!
Amazing place to visit but beware of Flowers Tea scammers. If you don't want to buy don't taste their samples. Quite expensive actually they sell per gram.
A must visit on a trip to Shanghai. Narrow streets with lots of small shops and a unique atmosphere.

This market is such a delightful experience. It’s a great place for photos, trying street food, shopping and people watching. You can buy some unique souvenirs that you can’t find anywhere else. Tip: Sit down at the patio for a brief escape and a few beers at a quiet little restaurant just off Xiexu & Liyuan Road.
Nice little shops, if you like Ghibli stuff here you can find a Store with LOTS of it, good food, if you want a break from the huge super futuristic Shanghai city just go here.
Interesting collection of lanes with little shops and food stalls. A lot of touristy thinks but fun to explore, even though it's very busy and crowded.
Awesome alleys to get lost in. Many souvenir shops but also some cool street food and small bars.

Tianzifang is part of the old French concession area in Shanghai and is very different to other areas you will visit in the city. For the reason, I recommend to put it on your visit to Shanghai if you're a tourist. It's labrynth of small alleyways and old streets with a number of tourist shops and local food stalls all over the place. Great atmosphere here - and is a great place to stop and have a beer if you're tired of walking and travelling.

Such a cool area to visit in Shanghai, part of “the french concession” although Chinese don’t really know this term. This is a great place to try traditional foods and desserts, good for shopping and exploring a part of old Shanghai. We spent a few hours walking around. It’s great to visit before/after fuxing park
Glad to visit this place. We came late before the sunset!! I like their shops but pricey! You must try to get their food inside! I had some food and drink as well.
Really nice quarter, where you can explore some nice shops. Good for a walk.throu of around 1 Hour. Easy to reach by metro. Unfortunately today it was very crowded.

Lovely streets of old Shanghai. Cramped alleyways full of quirky shops and cafes. Very nice experience walking through the area but do expect lots of tourists and tourist traps. Nonetheless a great place to go and pick up some trinkets and have a drink.
Alleys with shops and restaurants in a old residential area. There are people living on the second floor. Definitely worth visiting.
Great place for a photo hunting and a glass of beer. Many souvenir shops but the price is a bit too high.
Tian Zi Fang is one of my favourite place to go whenever I visit Shanghai. Love there is so many small alley way in between. Alot of shops, restaurants, bars around. Love it
Like a traditional market in Shanghai, a lot of thing to see and buy here, I think this one only for tourist, local people don't come here for shopping!

Unique experience in Shanghai. Loved getting lost in the alleys and shopping around. Not difficult to find. Easily accessible by metro. Only advice is to shop around. I definitely paid twice for something that I found much cheaper at another store! Lol

Charming hipster neighborhood in the French concession. Whilst very commercialised with similar gift shops, the architecture never fails to impress. There are many western dining options and bars to soak in the atmosphere.
Tiny alley of tourist attraction, bustling with visitor, I’d suggest to visit early in the morning or weekdays so you can enjoy all the shop freely
Good street, worth to visit if you wanna buy any souvenirs or try some street-food for tourists

Great area to stroll around for souvenirs. It has nice bars as well. Popular with Chinese and foreigners a like. Easy access from line 9 dapuqiao station exit 1 Popular in day evening and night. It is also not that far to walk from TianZiFang to Xintiandi bar area (or grab a taxi or rental bike).
It is especially beautiful at night when you can stroll around the streets and enjoy the small shops and little bars...
An ancient village in the heart of Shanghai. Its a beautiful authentic old part of Shanghai that still looks unouched and is the best spot get some food and gift, also get lovely photoshoot.

There are a lot of specialty and local shops here. You'll be amazed about some of their creations. Lane 210 has the most equisite finds. It can be crowded due to its steep walkways but nevertheless, it's worth visiting.

Shikumen-a well reserved ancient shanghai domestic architecture mass. Yet it has becomes quite touristic nowadays. If you’re looking for a quiet neighbour to wander, then maybe it’s not your best choice. For hunting down souvenirs, I’ve got mine anyway.

While this spot was likely once a hub for arts and tradition, it now feels more like a tourist trap. The area has become overly commercial, with inflated prices on food and an overwhelming number of generic gift shops that can be found in other tourist areas. The weekend crowds made it difficult to enjoy any sense of culture or creativity; instead, it felt chaotic and impersonal.
Great little street to find a concentration of artisan, jewelry, typical chinese little object and other things. its colourful all around with plants growing over head.
A lot of nice little shops and quite some quirky bars, great place to hang around for a few hours and taste some of Shanghai's finest
Another tourism spot in Shanghai TZF. Back lanes shops and restaurants. beware over your head if you happen to enter this area. They are hanging wet clothes for drying.
A market interconnected by small lanes with many places to eat and shop. Overall nice vibe but the things available for sale can be expensive. Also it gets really crowded.

The place is very crowded during weekends. What I like is the specialty shops in the area. Very interesting and full of creative merchandise. A lot of food stalls and restaurants too. Worth spending an afternoon here.

Nice lovely unique area of Shanghai! it's like a lively small hidden town with narrow street full of tiny shops, bars and foodies spots! It can get very crowded on the weekends, go by evening for a more romantic atmosphere, definitely something you cant miss!
A place full of old culture There are lots of food and souvenirs along the way. I feel like being spellbound when I come here
Cool place with lots of little bars, many variety shops, street food and restaurants
Try to walk inside the alley rather than main commercial street. Too many repeated shop selling the same stuffs. If you found a noodle shop name 壹碗粉 please give it a try 😋.
Small shops is here with different products. They have local food . it is narrow stores near to each other. No entrance fee .
Very nice place to shop. There are plenty of souvenir shops such as white rabbit, workshop for lipsticks DIY, rabbit tea shops, silver jewelery shops etc
Great architecture, and a cool feel to the place. Not a lot of air flow, so its very hot. Most of the shops are pretty full of touristy stuff, very little actual substance.
Great nostalgic landmark. Fun to walk around, shops, shops, shops! Favorite revisit spot...

Pretty little alleyways that look like what you might imagine Shanghai to have once looked like. Lots of shops, restaurants and bars crammed into every nook and cranny. A few are worth a look. It's best seen at night due to the way it's lit up, which only adds to it's charm. Unfortunately, the downside to this is, it tends to be more crowded in the evening. In any case, it's well worth a visit!

Fantastic marketplace with little eateries tucked away in the inner squares. The menus I saw were in English, and the whole area is generally friendly to English speakers, but it is handy to keep your phone loaded with a translate app to be safe.

This is one of those old village / hutong areas that has been repurposed as a high-end shopping area. Some of it is overpriced but there are gems to be found. Negotiate if you can, but keep in mind this is primarily a tourist area now. There’s a few good coffee shops and restaurants springing up around here as well.
Great place to walk around with friends or family, very unique tourist spot in Shanghai

First time here, plan to see the architecture but ended up it’s a place for tourists too shop😅. Got myself a qipao for 300 RMB and flower tea which tasted v nice but I think a bit expensive. 100g for 120 RMB & free 20g. That’s S$21 for 120g of flower tea! 😅
Novelty tourist market with some tourist places to eat. Lots to see and explore.

Very run down. Dark, smelly alleys—the Chinese lamps were mostly damaged and half the shops were closed at 6pm. The open shops offer standard “souvenirs” like cheap scarfs. If you want to see a nice pedestrian shopping area, go to the Yuyuan bazaar or Xintiandi.
A great place for walking down a old town feeling of Shanghai filled with food, souvenir and several unique shops.

Maybe I missed the more meaningful parts of the place, but although there were many small and fun elements, there wasn’t really anything worth buying. It was a place where I wanted to find something to buy, but ended up a bit disappointed.
Extraordinary shopping and dining area. Many stores with all kind of foods, drinks, and handmade accessories.
Good place to walk around. Reminds me of bugis Street in Singapore. Don't think there is much to shop apart from trying different local snacks.
If you are looking for a place with souvenir shops, coffee shops, restaurants look no further!
Local trendy area in Shanghai, lots of local buildings renovated to become attractive area, must visit!
Nothing much, was done in about 45mins. However the mall directly opposite is way more interesting. With lots of good food choices. Tried the Roll ING cake, not worth the 1hr Q. But I had time.
Go there to do your shopping and to buy souvenirs. Food is amazing and prepare to haggle.. 😉 Mix with the locals, enjoy the experience and good luck!
Loved this place! I was there in 2014 and the atmosphere is perfect for the young and the elderly! I recommend to everyone. It is like a maze but there is so much to see and do!
It’s like entering a magical Diagon Alley. Filled with curios and artsy souvenirs. Unique and thoroughly delightful. Confession: I did go a little teapot crazy today.
Found a little bar in the middle and spent 3 hours there. 10/10 would recommend.

Great place to wander around for souvenirs, shopping, old style alleys, cafe's etc. Plenty of photo opportunites. My favourite women's clothes shop is Fanny's, the owner designs her own range which is beautiful and fits very well.

Tucked away in the heart of Shanghai's French Concession, Tianzifang is a treasure trove of artistic expression and cultural charm. This tiny arts district, hidden behind a nondescript entrance, is a secret garden waiting to be discovered. As you wander through Tianzifang's narrow alleys, you'll find yourself immersed in a world of creativity and innovation. The streets are lined with art studios, galleries, cafes, and bars, each one showcasing a unique aspect of Shanghai's artistic personality. Every building, every doorway, seems to tell a story of art, creativity, and dreams. Tianzifang is a melting pot of artistic expression, where traditional Chinese calligraphy and painting blend seamlessly with modern street art and installation art. The district is also a hub of music and dance, with bars and clubs hosting live performances that attract artists and music lovers from around the world. If you're an art enthusiast or simply looking to experience Shanghai's vibrant artistic scene, Tianzifang is an absolute must-visit destination. The district's unique blend of art, music, and culture will leave you enchanted and inspired by the city's creative energy

Tianzifang, a hidden gem in the bustling city of Shanghai, is a place where history and modernity coexist. As you enter the narrow alley, you are greeted by a mosaic of old brick houses, colorful graffiti, and quaint shops. You can sense the charm of old Shanghai in the details of the architecture, such as the shikumen-style gates, the tiled roofs, and the wooden windows. Among the many attractions in Tianzifang, there is one restaurant that catches my eye. It has a simple wooden door framed by bamboo fences, creating a cozy and rustic atmosphere. Inside, there are low wooden tables and bamboo chairs, where you can sit and savor the delicious food. The restaurant offers a variety of dishes, from traditional Shanghai cuisine to fusion dishes inspired by other cultures. The food is not only tasty but also beautifully presented, making it a feast for both the eyes and the palate. . .

My favourite place in the French Concession, perhaps even the whole of Shanghai is Tianzifang. It’s neighbourhood within the French Concession that is a absolute maze. A labyrinth of alleyways and lanes that is known for crafts, artisan cafes, art studios that exudes a chic vibe. It’s easy to get lost here in Tianzifang. In fact, I did indeed got lost, which I felt was the best way to discover Tianzifang. It’s a little maze. Sometimes it leads you to unfamiliar places, other times it leads you back to where you started. Sometimes the blur of shops confuses you and then you see a familiar cafe or a familiar sign. If art inspires you, Tianzifang is an enclave filled with arts, design studios and crafts that would keep you here for hours. In fact, Tianzifang’s development from an old shikumen residence only started with a famed artist opened his studio in an abandoned factory buildings at Lane 210. Since then, this is where the artistic side of Shanghai blossoms. Tianzifang to me felt organic. Adds to why I loved its flavour. Preserving its original shikumen buildings (instead of being rebuilt like in nearby Xintiandi) and its growth organic, there’s a sense of a beautiful mess at work here. Past stalls selling sweet treats are local residents still living here in their homes.

À Xi'an par ex j'ai trouvé 1 boutique d'articles vraiment uniques, anciens, mais à prix faramineux, le touriste post covidien est désormais attendu à coup de bambou ! Éventuellement quartier à faire de jour pour se repérer et étendre aux alentours vers la concession française, ne pas faire comme moi arrivée la nuit tombée, après galère pour trouver 1 taxi depuis les grosses artères entourant le vieux Shanghai lui aussi transformé en dysney Land , puis 1 café avec des prises non uniquement chinoises pour recharger mon tél comme quoi dans les rues adjacentes c'est très chinois, fréquenté exclusivement par de jeunes chinois ... Évitez de venir exprès dans cette zone éloignée de l'hyper centre, sauf si vous avez vraiment du temps à perdre et êtes prêt à dépenser autant sinon plus qu'à Paris, pour bruncher puis aller voir plus loin dans la concession si c'est mieux ! Même la rue Nankin est plus intéressante.... Xintiandi est plus chic, classe, aéré, arboré, évidemment pas bon marché mais c'est clair... alors qu'ici ça se veut authentique, typique mais c'est un faux popu artificiel, cher et pas génial !

Tianzifang, situato nell’ex Concessione Francese di Shanghai, è un quartiere vivace ricavato da antiche case shikumen. Oggi ospita gallerie d’arte, botteghe artigianali, caffè e ristoranti, mantenendo il fascino delle sue strette viuzze storiche. È un luogo che unisce tradizione e modernità, rappresentando perfettamente lo spirito creativo della città.
日本人にもとても合う雰囲気だと思います。 香水や海外ブランドの服、石鹸、お土産、飲食店など何でも揃っていて、見て回るだけでも楽しいです。 中は少し迷路のような作りですが、その分探検気分を味わえます。 客引きもなく、自分のペースでゆっくり楽しめました。 値引き交渉をしてみるのも旅の思い出になるかもしれません。

Una bellissima passeggiata nel quartiere della Concessione Francese per inoltrarci nella zona “bohemienne” della città: Taikang Lu. Conosciuta anche come Tianzifang, questa via è un'oasi creativa e culturale, le strette strade sono fiancheggiate da edifici tradizionali, dove si trovano numerosi negozi e gallerie d'arte, boutique di moda, caffè e ristoranti accoglienti.

30분에서 한시간이면 충분한 작은 상점가 신톈디 들리는 날 동선에 끼우기 만만함. 여기서 블렌버니는 정말 괜찮아요. 쇼핑 할만한 퀄리티의 제품들. 포장도 좋고, 돌아가서도 잘 쓸 것 같네요. 1930년대 느낌의 챰 장식이 달린 토끼와 동방명주가 있는 찻잎 우리는 제품 제일 마음에듬. 그리고 그냥 평범한 기념품들도 살 수 있어요.

Ein schöner und gemütlicher Ort für einen Ausflug. Natürlich ist es touristisch gestaltet und es gibt viele Geschäfte. Aber auch nette Restaurant mit guten Getränken und Essen. Beim Einkaufen kann man ein bisschen verhandeln. Mir hat es gefallen und ich komme wieder.

さいっくぅーーーーーのChina雰囲気をあなたは！ここで！感じることができます！💐💐地下鉄9号線「打浦橋駅」を降りてふらっと歩いていくと到達します。視界に入った瞬間にうわぁーー、すげぇーーー、これやーーー！わたしが求めてたのは！って心の中がうきうきしてしまいます！ 田子坊は昔ながらの中国の雰囲気を残しており、ノスタルジックでアンニュイでエネルギッシュな感じです🇨🇳 お土産を買うのもよき！耳かきするのもよき！お茶のテイストするのもよし！写真撮りに来るだけでもよき！絶対よきです！ 上海きたら絶対絶対ぜーーーーったいに来たほうがいいです！

La zona está bien pero a una pena que se haya orientado todo al turista. Es una zona de antiguo asentamiento francés con callejuelas muy estrechas y en su momento tuvo que tener su encanto como algo poco común en la ciudad de Shanghai. Hoy en día como digo todo orientado al turismo, cafés, comida, souvenirs… 😊

上海にある田子坊に行ってみました。 地下鉄9号線の駅近くにありました。 地下鉄駅の上にはショッピングモールがあって、UNIQLOもあります。 田子坊は昔のアジアって感じで、狭い路地に小さなお店が並んでいるような感じです。 お茶、アイス等の軽食、お土産屋さんが沢山あります。 路地は狭いので、普通に歩くだけでも、ぶつからない様に気を付けて歩く感じなので、急いで移動は出来ません。 また、欧米の方も結構見かけましたので、それなりに有名な観光地だと思いました。 お土産は、田子坊独自のものは無さそうで、中国、上海の物になってそうでした。 もう少し田子坊をアピールするようなお土産があっても良い気がしました。 古いアジア感を味わうには良い所だと思いました。
旧区画を再整備して、オシャレ風に仕上げてます。 ネオがやや大人向けの遊び場に見えるのは私だけの感覚がおかしいとは思っていない。 次はぎの設計で雨水がところところに漏れてくるのはなんとかしてほしい。 ちなみに、上に大屋根をつけると、太陽光が入ってこれなくなるから、雰囲気がなくなる。
上海の新旧が入り交じった街を再現するような観光すボット田子坊🎶 上海の昔ながらの街並みを残しながら、アーティスティックであり、おしゃれなカフェやセレクトショップ、お土産屋なども立ち並ぶ人気観光スポットのようです‼️ 25年前はそこまで有名ではなかったと記憶しております。 周辺の町並みと異なりノスタルジックな雰囲気ですが、昔の上海を知っている、私にはちょっとピンとこなかったかなぁ～
地下鉄９号「打浦橋」駅からすぐ。おしゃれスポットでした。他にはないお土産もあり、ここで迷わず買っておいた方が良かったなって思うものもあり、上海観光おすすめスポットの１つでした。
